newsitem.title: UK: London exchange declines comment on Go-Ahead Group.
newsitem.headline: London exchange declines comment on Go-Ahead Group.

text.p: The London Stock Exchange (LSE) on Tuesday refused to confirm or deny that it was conducting an inquiry into recent share dealing in Go-Ahead Group Plc.

Labour MP Dale Campbell-Savours told the British parliament on Monday that the UK bus operator was being investigated by the LSE since it was shortlisted as a possible buyer of a railways franchise last November.
"We never comment on whether or not we are investigating one of our members," an LSE spokeswoman told Reuters. "I can say, however, that we always look at any unusual price movement in our shares."

Go-Ahead's shares have risen over 40 percent since GOVIA, a consortium of Go-Ahead, a management team and French group Via-GTI, was shortlisted by the British government for the Regional Railways North East franchise.
Go-Ahead has a 60 percent stake in Victory Railway Holdings, which won the franchise on September 19 to run the Thames Trains franchise.

Go-Ahead Group was down 12p at 494-1/2p by 0940 GMT in thin volume of 14,292 shares. "We've seen a few sellers on the stock exchange news but this is more of a mark down than anything else," one dealer said.
